Mobile Legends emblems and talents: what to upgrade and how to choose

Spend fragments where they help, match the emblem to your lane and choose three talents. See examples for Miya, Nolan, Vexana, Tigreal and more.

In this story

  1. Which emblem should you upgrade first?
  2. All 7 emblems and what each is for
  3. How to choose three talents for your hero
  4. Build examples for all five lanes
  5. Which emblems show up most often in builds?
All news
In this story
Which emblem should you upgrade first?All 7 emblems and what each is forHow to choose three talents for your heroBuild examples for all five lanesWhich emblems show up most often in builds?

In brief

  • The Common Emblem is enough to start. Once you have a main hero pool, upgrade the set you use most often on those heroes.
  • Assassin is a first candidate for junglers and burst heroes. Start with Mage for mid and choose between Tank and Support for roam.
  • One emblem provides base stats. You also select 3 talents, one from each row. Once unlocked, talents can be used with other emblems.

Which emblem should you upgrade first?

  1. Pick the heroes you play most and inspect their emblems in Preparation or on their hero pages. If several benefit from the same base stats, put your shared resources there.
  2. Use the Common Emblem while trying different roles. Unlock talents in other sets as you settle on your main heroes.
  3. Spend set-specific fragments on their matching set. Use shared Magic Dust to unlock a talent you need or to strengthen an emblem you equip regularly.
  4. Check the emblem screen before upgrading. It shows what the next level adds and where the talent you want unlocks. Use that to decide whether to max one set or invest in another.

All 7 emblems and what each is for

Emblem sets and typical uses
EmblemWhen to use it
CommonFor resource regeneration, extra health and a flexible starting point.
AssassinFor penetration and mobility. It can also suit magic-damage heroes who rely on a short burst combo.
MageWhen the build relies on magic power, magic penetration and shorter skill cooldowns.
FighterFor extended trades on skill-based heroes who benefit from spell vamp.
TankWhen you take the first hit and need health and hybrid defense.
SupportWhen the hero heals or protects allies and benefits from cooldown reduction.
MarksmanWhen frequent basic attacks deliver most of your damage and you need attack speed.

How to choose three talents for your hero

  1. In the first row, pick a stat that fits how the hero attacks. Swift helps when you need attack speed. Rupture helps when you need penetration.
  2. In the second row, choose an effect for the job you do. Seasoned Hunter helps a jungler contest neutral objectives. Wilderness Blessing suits roamers who spend time in the river and jungle.
  3. In the third row, read the trigger. Lethal Ignition suits quick burst combos. Focusing Mark fits heroes who regularly tag a target for teammates to follow up on.

Open Preparation from the lobby and inspect your available emblems and talents. Save the build on the hero you plan to play and check it before the match. If a talent is greyed out, open its card to see the unlock requirement.

Frequently asked questions

Which emblem is the most versatile?

Common is a handy starting set for regeneration and health. Once you have main heroes, look for the stats that help them do their job.

Can I use a Mage talent with the Assassin Emblem?

Yes, if you’ve unlocked it. The equipped emblem supplies the base stats. Talents are selected separately, one per row.

Why do players use different emblems on the same hero?

They may play different lanes, buy different items or prioritize different stats. Compare builds on the same lane and check when each talent triggers in your setup.
